_doc: Ports as places and the working boats (systems/ports.js, world/ferries.js, systems/barges.js; drawn by ui/innerMapPort.js + ui/innerMapLayers/portLife.js on the street map and ui/renderer/waterTraffic.js on the world map). harbour: berths by town size, the harbour dues the harbourmaster takes when one of your ships makes port (per cargo hold, per hand of crew, × the town's size; lighters' fee when every berth is taken: roadsMult; nothing in a port of your own realm or holding). yard: a ship on the slip goes up stage by stage (share = the share of the build days), each day drawing its stage's timber, planks, pitch, rope and sailcloth from the town's market (goods per 100 gold of the ship's base cost, a share a day) — none to be had and the work waits, up to maxStall of the build days. careen: hull repair over days, the ship out of service: a beach careening anywhere with shipwrights, a dry dock in the cities (or a port with your shipyard); rate = hull % a day, costShare of the instant repair bill, goods per 10 hull %. fishing: the boats of a port's fishers (one per fisher, or boatsBySize without a roster), out at dawn and back in the afternoon; a storm or the ice keeps them in, and the market's fish falls by the days lost (marketDynamics crew hook). ferries: across the great rivers near towns (range, spacing; share of the crossing's cost on foot / as a host / an army; fare; timetable hours) and over the straits between port towns on different landmasses (maxWater hexes; fare; a day's crossing). barges: the river links' trade drawn as barges with what really moved (render only).
